core_meaning.primary_meaning: Hakam corresponds to the Arabic form حَكَم and is glossed in this record as “A judge, arbiter, one who decides.” The record associates the form with root ح ك م (ḥ-k-m). The lexical gloss describes the word-form; Qur’anic occurrence, religious recommendation, popularity, and a name-bearer’s character are separate claims and are not established by this gloss alone.
core_meaning.literal_meaning: A judge, arbiter, one who decides
core_meaning.meaning_explanation: Hakam corresponds to the Arabic form حَكَم (Arabic root ح ك م (ḥ-k-m); حَكَم (ḥakam)). Its core sense is judge, arbiter, one who decides justly. Hakam is Arabic حَكَم (ḥakam) 'a judge, arbiter, one who decides'; the root ح ك م 'to judge, decide' is central to the Qur'anic vocabulary. The source gloss 'just judge' is defensible.
